payload.statement_nl: Let n > 1 and let f_n be defined as above. For any real r with 0 <= r < 1, if m = floor(n*r), then f_n(r) <= f_n(m/n).

result_payload.addressed_previous_feedback: Previous feedback indicated the argument was already correct: for r in [0,1), with m = floor(nr), each term floor(kr) dominates floor(km/n) by monotonicity of floor, so subtracting the sum gives f_n(r) <= f_n(m/n). This revision keeps that valid proof skeleton and states the floor-monotonicity comparison explicitly and cleanly.
result_payload.proof_nl:
Fix an integer n > 1, and define f_n(x) = floor(nx) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k. Let r be any real number with 0 <= r < 1, and set m = floor(nr). We must show f_n(r) <= f_n(m/n).

Since m = floor(nr), we have m <= nr < m+1. Dividing by n > 0 gives m/n <= r. Therefore, for each integer k with 1 <= k <= n, multiplying by k preserves the inequality:
k(m/n) <= kr.
Because the floor function is monotone nondecreasing on R, it follows that
floor(k(m/n)) <= floor(kr)
for every k = 1, ..., n.

Also, m is an integer, so
floor(n(m/n)) = floor(m) = m = floor(nr).

Now compare the two values:
f_n(r) = floor(nr) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(kr)/k
<= m - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k(m/n))/k
= floor(n(m/n)) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k(m/n))/k
= f_n(m/n).

This is exactly the desired inequality.
result_payload.proof_summary: For m = floor(nr), we have m/n <= r. Hence k(m/n) <= kr for each 1 <= k <= n, so floor(k(m/n)) <= floor(kr). Also floor(n(m/n)) = m. Substituting these into the definition of f_n yields f_n(r) <= f_n(m/n).
